Metadata.title: intellij-deodorant-reborn — Code Clone Detection Plugin
Metadata.description: Open-source IntelliJ IDEA plugin for detecting and refactoring Type-1 and Type-2 code clones in Java projects. Topology-aware, automated refactoring integrated directly into the IDE.

Hero.description: Open-source IntelliJ IDEA plugin for detecting and refactoring Type-1 and Type-2 code clones in Java projects — topology-aware automated refactoring integrated directly into the IDE.

Features.heading: Everything you need to fight code duplication
Features.subheading: A research-backed toolkit integrated directly into your IntelliJ workflow.
Features.type1Description: Identifies identical code fragments that differ only in whitespace, layout, and comments — across your entire Java project.
Features.type2Description: Finds syntactically similar code that differs in identifiers, literals, or types — catching near-duplicates that manual review would miss.
Features.refactoringDescription: Topology-aware refactoring: Extract Method within the same class, Pull Up to a shared superclass, or extract to a dedicated utility class — with a confirmation dialog before any change.
Features.ideDescription: Runs inside IntelliJ IDEA as a first-class plugin with a dedicated Tool Window — no external tools, command-line setup, or build changes required.
Features.incrementalDescription: Analysis results are cached between runs. Re-running detection on an unchanged codebase completes in about one second — no matter how large the project.
Features.researchDescription: Built on peer-reviewed clone detection research. Every detection heuristic is documented and traceable back to academic literature.

About.title: About intellij-deodorant-reborn
About.subtitle: A research-driven, open-source tool to eliminate code clones from Java projects — built as a portfolio thesis project.
About.originP1: intellij-deodorant-reborn is a modernised fork of IntelliJDeodorant, originally developed by the Software Analysis and Intelligence Lab at Concordia University. The original plugin pioneered automated detection and refactoring of code clones inside IntelliJ IDEA, but its development stalled with an outdated API and no active maintenance.
About.originP2: This project was born as a Bachelor thesis to breathe new life into that research: updating the plugin to the current IntelliJ Platform SDK, improving clone detection accuracy, and building a community platform around it so the work remains relevant and maintainable.
About.whatIntro: The plugin analyses Java source files inside IntelliJ IDEA and:
About.whatItem1: Detects Type-1 clones — identical code blocks differing only in whitespace, layout, or comments.
About.whatItem2: Detects Type-2 clones — syntactically similar blocks differing in identifiers, literals, or types.
About.whatItem3: Selects the right refactoring strategy based on class topology: Extract Method (same class), Extract & Pull Up (shared superclass), or Extract Utility Class — with a confirmation dialog before any structural change.
About.whatItem4: Integrates seamlessly via a dedicated IntelliJ Tool Window — no external tools or build changes needed.
About.whatItem5: Caches analysis results between runs — re-detection on an unchanged codebase completes in about one second.
About.authorRole: Bachelor graduate in Software Engineering · Based in Germany
About.authorBio: I built intellij-deodorant-reborn as my Bachelor thesis project, combining my passion for static analysis, developer tooling, and open-source software. The goal was not just to submit a thesis, but to ship a real tool that developers can actually install and use — and to document the process as a public portfolio.
About.techPlugin2: PSI (Program Structure Interface) for AST analysis
About.techPlugin3: Dedicated Tool Window (JBTable) + PMD CPD 7 integration
About.contributeP1: intellij-deodorant-reborn is fully open source under the MIT License. Contributions of all kinds are welcome: bug reports, feature requests, documentation improvements, or code.
About.contributeP2: The plugin and platform repositories are on GitHub. See the issues tab for open tasks — or open a new issue if you have an idea.
About.researchP1: The clone detection algorithms implemented in this plugin are based on the following peer-reviewed publications:
About.researchItem1: Roy, C. K. & Cordy, J. R. (2007). "A Survey on Software Clone Detection Research." Technical Report, Queen's University.
About.researchItem2: Tsantalis, N. et al. (2018). "IntelliJDeodorant: Identification and Application of Extract Method Refactoring." ICSE-C.
About.researchItem3: Fowler, M. (1999). "Refactoring: Improving the Design of Existing Code." Addison-Wesley.

research.topic1Desc: Extend detection beyond Type-1 and Type-2 to near-miss (Type-3) clones with added, removed, or modified statements while keeping refactoring safe.
research.topic2Desc: Adapt the topology-aware analysis and refactoring engine to Kotlin so mixed Java/Kotlin projects benefit from the same tooling.
research.topic3Desc: Build a reproducible benchmark suite to measure detection accuracy and refactoring latency on large real-world codebases.
